source_text: Ταῦτα συνεχῶς λέγω, καὶ λέγων οὐ παύσομαι. Τί γὰρ ὄφελος, ἁπλῶς καὶ εἰκῆ τρέχειν ἐνταῦθα, μηδὲν τῶν χρησίμων μανθάνοντας; ποῖον δὲ κέρδος, ἀεὶ τὰ πρὸς χάριν ὁμιλεῖν; Βραχὺς ὁ παρὼν καιρὸς, ἀγαπητοί· νήψωμεν, γρηγορήσωμεν, συγκροτήσωμεν ἑαυτοὺς, πᾶσαν σπουδὴν περὶ πάντας γνησίαν ἐπιδειξώμεθα, περὶ πάντα γενώμεθα εὐλαβεῖς· κἂν ἀκροᾶσθαι δέοι τῶν θείων λογίων, κἂν εὔχεσθαι, κἂν προσιέναι, κἂν ἕτερόν τι ποιεῖν, μετὰ φόβου καὶ τρόμου τοῦτο γινέσθω, ἵνα μὴ κατάραν ἐπισπασώμεθα διὰ τῆς ῥᾳθυμίας. Ἐπικατάρατος γὰρ, φησὶ, πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀμελῶς. Ὁ θόρυβος καὶ ἡ ὀργὴ ὕβρις εἰς τὴν προκειμένην θυσίαν γίνεται. Καταφρόνησις ἐσχάτη, μεμολυσμένον ἑαυτὸν προσενέγκαι τῷ Θεῷ. Ἄκουσον τί περὶ τῶν τοιούτων φησὶν ὁ Ἀπόστολος· Εἴ τις τὸν ναὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ φθείρει, φθερεῖ τοῦτον ὁ Θεός. Μὴ τοίνυν ἀντὶ καταλλαγῆς παροξύνωμεν τὸν Θεὸν, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν ἐπιμέλειαν καὶ πάντα κόσμον ἐπιδεικνύμενοι, καὶ ἀταραξίαν ψυχῆς, μετ' εὐχῆς καὶ συντετριμμένης καρδίας προσίωμεν, ἵνα καὶ αὐτῷ τούτῳ τὸν Δεσπότην ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἐξιλεωσάμενοι, δυνηθῶμεν ἐπιτυχεῖν τῶν ἐπηγγελμένων ἡμῖν ἀγαθῶν, χάριτι καὶ φιλανθρωπίᾳ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, μεθ' οὗ τῷ Πατρὶ, ἅμα τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, δόξα, κράτος, τιμὴ, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ, καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.
orientation: Chrysostom is concluding his homily with a final exhortation to approach the Eucharist with fear, order, and purity.
pass_a_gloss: These things I say continually, and saying them I will not stop. For what is the benefit, simply and at random to run in here, learning nothing of the useful things? And what is the gain, always to converse about things for favor? Short is the present time, beloved; let us be sober, let us watch, let us strengthen ourselves, let us show all genuine zeal concerning all people, let us become reverent concerning all things; and if it is necessary to listen to the divine oracles, and if to pray, and if to approach, and if to do any other thing, with fear and trembling let this happen, so that we do not draw down a curse upon ourselves through carelessness. For cursed, it says, is everyone who does the work of the Lord negligently. The disorder and the anger become an outrage against the sacrifice that is set before us. It is the utmost contempt, to bring oneself defiled to God. Hear what the Apostle says about such people: If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy this one. Therefore let us not provoke God instead of reconciliation, but showing all care and all order, and tranquility of soul, with prayer and a contrite heart let us approach, so that having propitiated our Master Jesus Christ by this very thing, we may be able to obtain the good things promised to us, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ himself, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

lemmas.gloss: let us draw down upon ourselves

choices.english: simply and at random to run in here
choices.why: Keeps the adverbial force of ἁπλῶς and εἰκῆ as describing careless, purposeless movement, matching the rhetorical question's criticism of mindless attendance.
rejected: to run here thoughtlessly and without purpose
to come here casually and haphazardly

choices.english: to converse about things for favor
choices.why: Preserves the sense of speaking to please or flatter rather than to benefit, which fits the contrast with learning useful things.
The verb συγκροτέω here means to brace or fortify oneself, fitting the hortatory series of soberness and watchfulness.
The middle voice with κατάραν conveys bringing a curse upon oneself, and 'draw down' keeps the spatial metaphor of the compound.

choices.term: ὕβρις εἰς τὴν προκειμένην θυσίαν γίνεται
choices.english: become an outrage against the sacrifice that is set before us
choices.why: ὕβρις is strong, denoting insolent violence or outrage, and προκειμένην refers to the sacrifice placed before the congregation, so 'set before us' preserves the liturgical sense.
rejected: an insult to the sacrifice at hand
a violation of the present offering

choices.why: ἀταραξία is the Stoic term for undisturbed calm, and rendering it 'tranquility' keeps the philosophical resonance while fitting the liturgical context.

bible_refs.note: Ἐπικατάρατος πᾶς ὁ ποιῶν τὸ ἔργον τοῦ Κυρίου ἀμελῶς

pass_b_english: I say these things constantly, and I will not stop saying them. For what is the benefit of simply and at random running in here, learning none of the useful things? And what is the gain of always conversing about things for favor? The present time is short, beloved. Let us be sober, let us watch, let us strengthen ourselves. Let us show every genuine effort toward all people, and let us be reverent in everything. Whether we must listen to the divine oracles, or pray, or approach, or do anything else, let it be done with fear and trembling, so that we do not draw down a curse upon ourselves through carelessness. For it says, “Cursed is everyone who does the work of the Lord negligently” (Jeremiah 48:10 LXX). The uproar and the anger become an outrage against the sacrifice that is set before us. It is the utmost contempt to bring oneself defiled to God. Listen to what the Apostle says about such people: “If anyone destroys the temple of God, God will destroy that person” (1 Corinthians 3:17). Therefore let us not provoke God instead of being reconciled, but let us show every care and all good order, and tranquility of soul, and let us approach with prayer and a contrite heart, so that by this very thing we may propitiate our Master Jesus Christ and be able to obtain the good things promised to us, by the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ himself, with whom to the Father, together with the Holy Spirit, be glory, might, honor, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.why: "Things for favor" misrepresents τὰ πρὸς χάριν, which means pleasant/flattering speech, not seeking favor.
last_rejected.ruling: τὰ πρὸς χάριν means things conducive to favor/pleasing; 'things for favor' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: uproar and the anger become an outrage against the sacrifice
last_rejected.source_quote: Ὁ θόρυβος καὶ ἡ ὀργὴ ὕβρις εἰς τὴν προκειμένην θυσίαν γίνεται
last_rejected.why: ὕβρις is the subject: "uproar and anger ARE an outrage toward the sacrifice," not "become."
last_rejected.fix: Uproar and anger are an outrage against the sacrifice set before us
last_rejected.ruling: γίνεται with predicate ὕβρις can mean 'become'; 'become an outrage' is within normal Greek usage.

last_rejected.why: Infinitive depends on καταφρόνησις: "It is utmost contempt TO bring oneself defiled to God"—but "bring oneself" obscures that one offers/presents oneself.
last_rejected.fix: It is the utmost contempt to present oneself defiled to God
last_rejected.ruling: προσενέγκαι means bring/present; 'bring oneself defiled' adequately renders the reflexive ἑαυτὸν without meaning loss.
